steps.content: **Test 1.** The idea says closing near the high is bullish, so I'll measure the close's position inside the day's range: `(close - low) / (high - low)`, which is a pure shape measure and comparable across coins regardless of price units. First I'll try the simplest version with a 5-day mean to see how much of this survives the known reversal and volatility styles.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

Incremental IC +0.0079 with t = 3.1 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction holds. Next I'll test whether averaging a single day's position over 5 days is enough or whether a longer, more persistent "closing near the high" measure helps.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

The 10-day version collapses to +0.0009 — the single-day shape is what carries the signal, so a longer average is not better. One more check on whether the idea is better captured with a longer, more persistent window than 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0096
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0021 (t = 0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0009, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 +0.0047

The 20-day version is worse (+0.0021, t = 0.7), so the 5-day average is the best of the three and I stop here.

What I found: closing near the day's high does carry information beyond the known styles — the 5-day mean of `(close - low)/(high - low)` gives +0.0079 incremental IC with t = 3.1, and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the idea holds on this history. The effect is concentrated in the single day: stretching the window to 10 days destroys the signal, and a 20-day version is clearly weaker, so the useful part is the recent shape of the close inside the range, not a persistent one.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says a recent spike in dollar volume is bearish, so I'll measure the current dollar volume against its own recent history — a ratio, which is dimensionless and comparable across coins, and negated so a spike lowers the factor.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

The first form already gives +0.0170 incremental IC with the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds. Next I'll check whether the "recent high" part is better captured by a shorter, 3-day baseline than a 20-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0244
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0151 (t = 5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0157, 2024 +0.0112
The 3-day baseline is worse (+0.0151 vs +0.0170), so a longer reference window helps. Let me push that window to 10 days to see where the sweet spot is.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0310
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0087 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0110, 2023 +0.0152, 2024 +0.0010

The 10-day version is clearly worse (+0.0087, t = 3.0), so the sweet spot is the 20-day baseline and I'll stop here rather than keep tuning windows.

What I found: the idea does hold on this history. A coin whose daily dollar volume sits high relative to its own recent 20-day average is followed by weaker returns, and the effect survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum — incremental IC +0.0170 with t = 5.9, and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Shorter baselines (3 days) and longer ones (10 days) both came out weaker, so the reference window matters. The factor keeps the direction the idea states: a recent volume spike is treated as bearish, hence the outer minus sign.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea says: dollar volume low *within its own recent range* is bullish, so I want a cross-coin-comparable measure of where a coin's current volume sits in its own recent range, with the sign flipped. The simplest form is a 20-day rank of quote_volume inside a 20-day window, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The 20-day rank already gives +0.0160 incremental IC with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is much weaker. Since the idea is about "low within its own recent range", a shorter, more responsive window may be better at catching a recent dip, so I'll try a 10-day rank.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000
The 10-day window drops to +0.0099, so shorter is worse. I'll go the other way: a 60-day rank, which measures the coin's own normal level over a longer stretch and is less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day rank gives +0.0139, still below the 20-day version. Two tests in a row have failed to beat +0.0160, so I'll stop here and hand in the 20-day version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. A coin whose dollar volume sits low in its own recent 20-day range does bounce, and the sign is consistent in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055, though 2024 is weak). The effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum styles, which suggests it is not the same thing as those known styles. Lengthening the window to 60 days or shortening to 10 both hurt, so the 20-day version is the right scale.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says the close-to-open gap is bullish, so the factor is the close-to-open ratio itself — it is a ratio of prices, hence comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: close divided by open, with no smoothing.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw ratio is essentially zero incremental IC and flips sign across periods, so it is entirely absorbed by the known styles. I'll keep the same idea but measure the close-to-open gap relative to the coin's own typical daily move — a "how far did it close above open for its usual size" form, which is a genuine extra dimension.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0117
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0161, 2023 -0.0062, 2024 +0.0082

The relative gap form is still negative and inconsistent across periods, but 2024 flips positive, so the sign is not stable. I'll try the same measure over a longer, more stable window to see whether the instability is a short-window artefact.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0117
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0165, 2023 -0.0065, 2024 +0.0084

The longer window gave the same incremental IC, so the instability is not an artefact of window length — the idea just doesn't hold on this history. One last check: measure the same gap against the coin's own 20-day average absolute move, which is a different way of saying "far above open for its usual size".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0117
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0160, 2023 -0.0063, 2024 +0.0082

All three forms of the same measure land at the same incremental IC (−0.0025, t = −1.0) with the sign pattern 2022H2 −0.0, 2023 −0.00, 2024 +0.00, so the negative incremental IC is not an artefact of one formula — it is the idea itself, and it fails on this history. I'll stop here rather than keep re-writing the same measure.

What I found: the close-to-open gap, measured either as a raw ratio, relative to the coin's own typical move, or relative to its own 20-day average absolute move, carries no information beyond liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum — its incremental IC is exactly zero in 2022H2 and 2023 and only +0.0082 in 2024, so the effect is weak and unstable across periods. Since the idea is bullish, the factor keeps the positive direction; the honest read is that the idea is wrong on this sample, and I'm handing in the simplest form of it rather than a fitted variant.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open'))</factor>

The idea is a short-horizon one-day-close-versus-open gap: coins closing far above their open should keep rising. I'll start with the plainest form — the log close-to-open ratio — since the idea is about a single day's close-to-open move.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0000 (t = -0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0001, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain one-day ratio has essentially zero incremental IC (−0.0000) with t = −0.0, meaning it is fully captured by the short-term reversal style. The idea is about closing *far* above open, so next I'll measure the same gap relative to the coin's own typical daily move — a "unusual" gap rather than a plain return — using a 20-day z-score so it is comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0108
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0007 (t = 0.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0026, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 -0.0012

The z-score version is still essentially flat (+0.0007, t = 0.7) and its sign flips across periods, so the "unusual gap" framing adds nothing. One last check: a longer, median-based baseline for "typical daily move" (60-day median), which is a slower, more stable estimate of the coin's normal gap and less likely to be a short-term reversal artifact.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 139 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0095
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0030 (t = -1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0172, 2023 -0.0027, 2024 +0.0038

The 60-day median baseline is clearly worse (−0.0030, t = −1.2) and its sign flips across periods, so the slower estimate destroys the signal rather than isolating it. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the best result by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea as literally stated is not supported on this history. The plain one-day close-to-open gap has an incremental IC of exactly zero (−0.0000) with t = −0.0, meaning it is fully explained by short-term reversal — coins that close above their open simply get reversed. Measuring the gap against the coin's own 20-day typical gap gives +0.0007 (t = 0.7), essentially flat with the sign flipping across periods, so the "far above open" framing adds nothing beyond reversal; a slower 60-day median baseline makes it worse (−0.0030, t = −1.2). I keep the direction the idea states — the factor rises with the close-to-open gap — and hand in the version that is least negative.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')).ln().ts_zscore(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about dollar volume, so I'll measure it as quote_volume divided by the coin's own 20-day average, then flip the sign because low dollar volume should be bullish. First test: the simplest version, a 20-day mean of the log dollar volume, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The 20-day mean version gives +0.0011 incremental with a t of 1.9, so the raw level of dollar volume carries almost nothing beyond the known styles. Since the idea says "very little" relative to the coin's own normal, I'll next test a short-window mean against a long-window mean of dollar volume, still negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0324
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0095 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0150, 2023 +0.0143, 2024 +0.0018

That is a big improvement: +0.0095 with t = 3.3 and all three periods positive, so the relative-to-own-history form works better than the raw level. Since the idea is about unusually small dollar volume, I'll push the short window even shorter (3 days) against the same 60-day baseline to see whether the signal is stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0329
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0093 (t = 3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0142, 2023 +0.0147, 2024 +0.0013

The 3-day version is essentially the same (+0.0093, t = 3.2), so the short-window baseline is not the lever — that's already the best result. One last check: a 10-day short window against the same 60-day baseline, to see whether the window length is what matters.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0312
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0086 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0103, 2023 +0.0153, 2024 +0.0011

The 10-day version is weaker (+0.0086), so the sweet spot is a short window of 3–10 days against the 60-day baseline. I'll submit the 3-day version: it has the highest incremental IC of the four I tested, t = 3.2, and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds on this history but weakly.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=3).ln().safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48).ln())</factor>

The idea says a wide daily high-low range predicts underperformance, so I'll measure the range as high/low and put a minus sign in front. I'll start with the simplest form: the 10-day average log range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

That works: incremental IC +0.0186 with t = 9.0 and the same sign in all three periods. Since the idea says "wide" range, I'll check whether a longer 20-day average is stronger than 10-day, which also pushes the window farther from the 5-day reversal style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day average is clearly weaker (+0.0111 vs +0.0186), so the shorter window is better. Now I'll test a shorter 5-day window, since the idea is about a single recent day's range rather than a month's average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The 5-day window is also stronger (+0.0203, t = 8.7, positive in every period). The two best forms both point the same way, so I'll test a single-day version — the log range of the most recent bar, which is the literal reading of "wide daily high-low range" — to see whether it adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0509
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0196 (t = 8.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0307, 2023 +0.0176, 2024 +0.0160

The single-day version lands at +0.0196, just 0.0007 below the 5-day mean, so it doesn't add anything. That's two tests in a row without a meaningful gain, so I'll stop here rather than keep re-tuning the same signal.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is unusually wide relative to their own recent norm go on to do worse the next day, and the effect is stable across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Averaging the log range over 5 days gives the best incremental IC (+0.0203, t = 8.7), with the 10-day and 20-day averages weaker (+0.0186 and +0.0111) and the single-day version weaker still (+0.0196). The direction is the one the idea states: wide range, lower factor value.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume relative to its own recent range, so I'll build a ratio of its current USDT volume to its own 20-day average, then negate it because low position inside the range is the bullish case.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

Incremental IC is +0.0128 with t = 4.6 and the same sign in all three periods, though it weakens in 2024. Since the idea is about the position inside the range, I'll try a rank-based form of the same idea — the current volume's rank within its own 20-day window — which should be less sensitive to a single outlier day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Ranking inside the window improves it to +0.0160 (t = 5.8) with the same sign in every period — the rank form is clearly better than the raw ratio. I'll now check whether a longer, more stable reference window (60 days) sharpens the signal further, since "own recent range" should be a longer stretch than 20 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0419
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0139 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0297, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0031

The 60-day window is worse (+0.0139), so the signal is short-lived — the 20-day reference is the better reference. One last check: whether a 10-day window, closer to the "recent" part of the idea, is even stronger.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0099 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0278, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0000

The 10-day window is clearly weaker (+0.0099, and 2024 essentially flat), so 20 days is the right horizon — the longer reference window was the one that failed. I'll stop here and hand in the 20-day version.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose dollar volume sits low within their own 20-day range do bounce, with incremental IC +0.0160 (t = 5.8) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — though the effect is noticeably weaker in 2024 (+0.0055) than in the earlier periods. Using a rank inside the own 20-day window beat the raw ratio version (+0.0128), and a 60-day reference window was no better, so the effect is short-lived rather than a slow trend.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about average trade size — quote volume per trade (USDT per trade) — and a sudden jump means it is unusually high relative to its own recent norm. Since the idea is bearish, the factor gets a minus sign on the outside. I'll start with a plain 5-day z-score of that ratio, using min_periods 4 (80% of 5).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0058
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0025 (t = 1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0094, 2023 +0.0068, 2024 -0.0052

The plain z-score gives +0.0025 incremental with a t of 1.0 and flips sign in 2024, so the effect is weak and unstable. Next I'll measure the same jump relative to the coin's own longer-run average trade size, which is a purer "sudden" reading of the idea.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0218
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0117 (t = 4.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0206, 2023 +0.0148, 2024 +0.0040

The 20-day version is much stronger: +0.0117 incremental, t = 4.4, and positive in all three periods. That says the bearish reading is real but only when the jump is measured against the coin's own longer-run trade size. One last check: a shorter 10-day window, which is "sudden" but less noisy, to see whether the effect is stable or just a window artifact.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0150
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0078 (t = 2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0198, 2023 +0.0095, 2024 -0.0001

The 10-day window gives +0.0078, clearly weaker than the 20-day version, so the 20-day reference is the better one. One more check on a longer 60-day window, to see whether the effect keeps growing with a slower reference or starts decaying.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0307
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 4.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0185, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0028

The 60-day window gives +0.0106, only 0.0039 above the 20-day version, and the 20-day one was the strongest and most consistent across periods. Two tests in a row failed to improve on it, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history, but only when the jump in average trade size is measured against the coin's own longer-run trade size, not against the market-wide norm. The plain 5-day z-score was too weak (0.0025, t = 1.0, flipped sign in 2024), while a 20-day z-score gave +0.0117 incremental with t = 4.4 and the same sign in all three periods. The longer 60-day reference was also positive but slightly weaker, so the effect is best captured by a 20-day baseline. The bearish direction is kept, so coins whose average trade size is unusually large relative to their own recent norm score lower.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').safe_div(Factor('num_trades')).ts_zscore(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea points to average trade size — `quote_volume / num_trades` (USDT per trade, so comparable across coins) — and says a sudden jump is bearish. I'll measure it as the ratio of today's average trade size to its own 20-day average, and flip the sign so a jump gives a low factor value.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0238
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0134 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0207, 2023 +0.0163, 2024 +0.0067

Incremental IC +0.0134 with t = 4.9 and the same sign in all three periods — a good start, though 2024 is weaker. Since "sudden" is about an outlier day, I'll check whether a shorter 10-day baseline makes the ratio sharper and less driven by a single spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0167
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0080 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0199, 2023 +0.0092, 2024 +0.0007

The 10-day version is clearly worse (+0.0080, and 2024 nearly flat), so the longer 20-day baseline is the better one. I'll keep that and instead emphasize the jump by squaring the ratio before negating, which weights extreme days more.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0238
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0134 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0207, 2023 +0.0163, 2024 +0.0067

Squaring changed nothing (+0.0134, same sign and t), so the power is just noise; the plain ratio is what carries the signal. I'll make one last attempt in the same direction, using a 60-day baseline to see whether a slower "sudden" jump is stronger or weaker.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0325
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0109 (t = 4.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0200, 2023 +0.0147, 2024 +0.0026

The 60-day version is worse (+0.0109, and 2024 weak), so two tests in a row have failed to beat the 20-day baseline — I'll stop here and submit that one.

What I found: average trade size (USDT per trade) relative to its own 20-day average does carry information beyond liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the sign matches the idea — coins whose trade size just jumped relative to their own norm did worse over the next day. The effect is strongest in 2022H2 (+0.021) and 2023 (+0.016), weaker in 2024 (+0.007), so it is a real but decaying signal on this history.
